items.title: A stop for a short position
items.prompt: You are short 40 shares, sold at £75.00. At price $p$ your P&L is $40(75 - p)$ pounds. Your risk desk caps the loss at £400.00, so the P&L must stay at or above $-400$. Find the prices at which you are within the limit, showing each step with its reason. Explain why one step reverses the inequality sign, and check your answer with two test prices. Then rearrange the P&L to give the price at which the loss reaches a general limit of $L$ pounds.
items.model:
**Setting up.** The rule is that P&L must be at least −400:

$$40(75 - p) \ge -400$$

**Solving, one move per line.**

$$\begin{aligned} 75 - p &\ge -10 &&\text{divide both sides by 40, a positive number, so the sign stays} \\ -p &\ge -85 &&\text{subtract 75 from both sides} \\ p &\le 85 &&\text{multiply both sides by } -1 \text{, which reverses the sign} \end{aligned}$$

You are within the limit while $p \le 85.00$. At exactly £85.00 the loss is £400.00, which is still allowed. You must close once the price rises above £85.00.

**Why the sign reverses.** Multiplying by $-1$ mirrors every number across 0 on the number line. Order flips in a mirror: $3 < 5$, but $-3 > -5$. So $-p \ge -85$ becomes $p \le 85$, never $p \ge 85$.

**Checks.** At $p = 80$: $40 \times (75 - 80) = -200$, which is above −400, so within the limit, and 80 satisfies $p \le 85$. At $p = 90$: $40 \times (75 - 90) = -600$, below −400, so outside, and 90 fails $p \le 85$. Both agree.

**General limit.** Set the P&L equal to $-L$ and make $p$ the subject:

$$\begin{aligned} 40(75 - p) &= -L \\ 75 - p &= -\tfrac{L}{40} &&\text{divide by 40} \\ p &= 75 + \tfrac{L}{40} &&\text{add } p \text{ and } \tfrac{L}{40} \text{ to both sides} \end{aligned}$$

With $L = 400$ this gives $p = 75 + 10 = 85$, as before. For a short of $n$ shares sold at $P_0$, the same steps give $p = P_0 + \tfrac{L}{n}$: a bigger position puts the stop closer to the entry.

rubric.text: Sets up the inequality $40(75 - p) \ge -400$ correctly.
Solves it to $p \le 85$ with a reason for every line.
Explains that multiplying by −1 reverses the order of numbers, so the sign reverses.
States the conclusion in trading terms: close above £85.00, with £85.00 itself allowed.
Checks with one price inside and one outside the solution set.
Rearranges to $p = 75 + \tfrac{L}{40}$ and checks it gives 85 when $L = 400$.
